2011 HWA Bram Stoker Award® for Superior Achievement in a Poetry Collection How To Recognize A Demon Has Become Your Friend. Cover & interior art by Jill Bauman.
2012 HWA Bram Stoker Award® finalist Dark Duet (with Stephen M. Wilson). Cover art by Kiri Moth, interior art by Jill Bauman.

2013 HWA Bram Stoker Award® for Superior Achievement in a Poetry Collection Four Elements (with Charlee Jacob, Marge Simon & Rain Graves). Cover art by Daniele Serra, interior art by Marge Simon, photo on page 135 by Jim Jacob.
2015 HWA Mentor of the Year Award Recognizes a mentor in the HWA Mentor Program who has done an outstanding job of helping newer writers.
2017 HWA Bram Stoker Lifetime Achievement Award Presented to an individual whose work has substantially influenced the horror genre.
2017 HWA Bram Stoker Award® Anthology finalist Sycorax’s Daughters edited with Kinitra Brooks, PhD & Susana Morris, PhD. Cover art by Jim Callahan.
2019 HWA Bram Stoker Award® for Superior Achievement in a Poetry Collection The Place of Broken Things (with Alessandro Manzetti). Cover art by Adrian Borda, interior art by Luke Spooner.

[2020 SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry](https://www.sfpoetry.com/gm/20grandmaster.html) From the Science Fiction and Fantasy Poetry Association to an individual whose body of work reflects the highest artistic goals of the SFPA, and whose poetry has been noted to be exceptional in merit, scope, vision and innovation.

[2021 Science Fiction and Fantasy Poetry Association (SFPA) Rhysling Awards](http://sfpoetry.com/ra/pages/21rhysling.html), First Place Short Poem category; for my poem "Summer Time(lessness)” first published in Star*Line Magazine 43.4.

2022 Science Fiction and Fantasy Poetry Association (SFPA) Rhysling Awards[http://sfpoetry.com/ra/pages/22rhysling.html], 3rd Place Short Poem category; for my poem "The Butterfly Affect” first published in Were Tales: A Shapeshifter Anthology edited by S.D. Vassal & Steven M. Long.

bio.content: Linda D. Addison grew up in Philadelphia and began weaving stories at an early age. Ms Addison is the first African-American recipient of the world renowned HWA Bram Stoker Award® and has received five awards for collections: *The Place of Broken Things* written with Alessandro Manzetti; *Four Elements* written with Charlee Jacob, Marge Simon and Rain Graves; *How To Recognize A Demon Has Become Your Friend* short stories and poetry; *Being Full of Light, Insubstantial;* *Consumed, Reduced to Beautiful Grey Ashes*. In 2018, she received the HWA Lifetime Achievement Award. In 2020, Addison was designated SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry.She co-edited *Sycorax's Daughters* anthology of horror fiction & poetry by African-American women with Kinitra Brooks PhD and Susana Morris PhD, which was a HWA Bram Stoker finalist in the Anthology category. She currently lives in Arizona and has published over 400 poems, stories and articles. Look for her story in the *Black Panther: Tales of Wakanda* anthology (Titan/Marvel).

Linda D. Addison grew up in Philadelphia and began weaving stories at an early age. Ms Addison is the first African-American recipient of the world renowned HWA Bram Stoker Award® and has received five awards for collections: *The Place of Broken Things* written with Alessandro Manzetti; *Four Elements* written with Charlee Jacob, Marge Simon and Rain Graves; *How To Recognize A Demon Has Become Your Friend* short stories and poetry; *Being Full of Light, Insubstantial;* *Consumed, Reduced to Beautiful Grey Ashes*. In 2018, she received the HWA Lifetime Achievement Award. In 2020, Addison was designated SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry.*Dark Duet,* a collaborative book of poetry written with Stephen M. Wilson was a HWA Bram Stoker finalist. She co-edited *Sycorax's Daughters*, an anthology of horror fiction & poetry by African-American women with Kinitra Brooks PhD and Susana Morris PhD, which was a HWA Bram Stoker finalist in the Anthology category. 

She is the only author with fiction in three landmark anthologies that celebrate African-Americans speculative writers: the award-winning anthology *Dark Matter: A Century of Speculative Fiction* (Warner Aspect), *Dark Dreams I* and *II* (Kensington), and *Dark Thirst* (Pocket Book). 

Her work has made frequent appearances over the years on the honorable mention list for Year's Best Fantasy and Horror and Year's Best Science-Fiction and has published over 400 poems, stories and articles. She has work in numerous publications, including *Essence* magazine, *Asimov's Science Fiction* magazine, *Weird Tales* magazine #364, *Miscreations* anthology, *Don't Turn Out the Lights* anthology and *The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction*. Look for her story in the *Black Panther: Tales of Wakanda* anthology (Titan/Marvel).

Linda is the second oldest of ten children and grew up in Philadelphia where she graduated from Germantown High School. Her childhood memories include evenings listening to her mother tell stories she created, using the children as characters or watching scary movies with her mother at night. 

From the first moment she held a book in her hands in kindergarten Ms. Addison knew she wanted to make one of her own. She graduated from Carnegie-Mellon University with a B.S. in Mathematics and currently lives in Arizona. 

Linda is a founding member of a writing group, Circles In The Hair (CITH) which started meeting in 1990. She is poetry editor for *Space & Time Magazine*. Her work has made frequent appearances over the years on the honorable mention list for *Year's Best Fantasy and Horror* and *Year's Best Science-Fiction.* 

In 2001, Addison was the first African-American to win the HWA's Bram Stoker Award® for superior achievement in poetry for *Consumed, Reduced to Beautiful Grey Ashes*. She has received four additional awards for collections: *Being Full of Light, Insubstantial; How To Recognize A Demon Has Become Your Friend,* short stories and poetry collection; *Four Elements* written with Marge Simon, Rain Graves and Charlee Jacob; and *The Place of Broken Things* written with Alessandro Manzetti.*Dark Duet*, written with Stephen M. Wilson, was a 2012 HWA Bram Stoker Award® finalist. She co-edited *Sycorax's Daughters*, an anthology of horror fiction & poetry by African-American women with Kinitra Brooks PhD and Susana Morris PhD, which was a HWA Bram Stoker Award® finalist. 

Linda D. Addison is the only author with fiction in three landmark anthologies that celebrate African-American speculative writers: the award-winning anthology *Dark Matter: A Century of Speculative Fiction* (Warner Aspect), *Dark Dreams I* and *II* (Kensington), and *Dark Thirst* (Pocket Book). 

Addison is a founding member of the writer's group Circles in the Hair (CITH) and a member of SFWA, HWA and SFPA. In 2018, she received the HWA Lifetime Achievement Award. In 2020, she was designated SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry. 

She has over 400 poems, stories and articles in print. Addison has work in numerous publications, including *Essence* magazine, *Asimov's Science Fiction* magazine, *Weird Tales* magazine #364, *Miscreations* anthology, *Don't Turn Out the Lights* anthology and *The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction*. Look for her story in the *Black Panther: Tales of Wakanda* anthology (Titan/Marvel).

Hi Linda, One of my oldest friends is Tucson-based poet Charles Alexander. Earlier today he sent this and I thought you might be interested:

Award and Invitation
Dear Friends & Colleagues,

I’m receiving a national award a week from today at 6:30pm EST, through CLMP, though it’s not their award. It is a private award begun several years ago in honor of Jonathan Williams & Jargon Books, and given to an editor/publisher for lifetime achievement. It is called the Lord Nose award, as apparently that was something Jonathan liked to sign at the end of notes, letters, etc. The program director for CLMP wrote me, "In addition to being given in memory of Jonathan Williams, the Lord Nose Award recognizes a lifetime of superlative small press publishing. It's given to publishers that achieved continued excellence in their work throughout their years of publication. The award recognizes the important contribution to the independent literary community that Chax Press has had and why it remains a press of inspiration. We're honored that you will be accepting it.” I’m honored, and excited. The award will be presented to me by David Wilk, who himself is a lifetime book worker & supporter I esteem very highly. The award is not something applied for, rather I received a surprise message that I was chosen for it.

If you want to forward this invitation to someone you think might be interested, please do.  

To register to attend (virtually — it’s all Zoom) the awards ceremony, which also includes the CLMP Firecracker awards for Fiction, Creative Nonfiction, Poetry, Magazines/General Excellence, and Magazines/Best Debut, please follow this link: https://centerforfiction.org/event/the-clmp-firecracker-awards/ 

Thank you all for your friendship and support!

With love,
Charles


Charles Alexander
Poet & Director, Chax Press

Ms. Addison,
My name is Gary Phillips. Along with my friend Gar Anthony Haywood, we're putting together an anthology for Soho Crime called Witnesses for the Dead. Your fellow Tales from Wakanda writer Chris Chamber has committed to do a story for the collection and we wanted to see if you would too.  There is pay and particulars are below. 

It's a night in March 1991 and George Holliday is awakened by the sounds of …he’s not quite sure what.  He grabs his bulky video camera and from the balcony of his apartment across the street, tapes the merciless beating of motorist Rodney King by members of the Los Angeles Police Department. On April 4, 2015, Feidin Santana is on his way to work in North Charleston and happens to witness an altercation with police officer Michael Slager and another motorist, Walter Scott. He uses his smartphone to capture the officer shooting Scott dead, in the back, as Scott attempts to run away.
Darnella Frazier is the eighteen-year-old black woman who, in video recording George Floyd's death at the hands (or rather, left knee) of Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin on May of 2020, helped lead to Chauvin's conviction on murder and manslaughter charges – and his eventual sentencing. People across the country, including Floyd's family, have applauded her bravery and quick thinking in the face of police pressure to leave the scene, which they say made the guilty verdict possible.
Like Ms. Frazier and the aforementioned, the characters who will populate the stories in Witnesses For the Dead will all find themselves in a similar, unenviable position -- a murder has been committed to which they have been an unwitting eyewitness, and just as Frazier did, they will choose taking action over doing nothing. Could be they have the homicide on video or more likely they don’t. But you'll find no passive bystanders here. Placing their own safety and welfare at risk, the men and women throughout Witnesses For the Dead will follow Darnella Frazier's lead and do whatever is necessary to see that the dead are avenged, the guilty are punished, and justice is served. It's either that or die trying.
The original tales for this anthology can be set today or in the past, may or may not involve law enforcement, domestic or on foreign shores. 4,500-8,000 words or thereabouts. Payment is a flat fee of $350 upon acceptance. The collection is to be published by Soho Crime. Deadline is December 15, 2021 but please let us knows as soon as possible if you’re in or out. The editors will commit any royalty proceeds to go toward a nonprofit advocating for active citizen engagement in social/legal justice issues.
Thank you for your consideration and any questions you may have, please don’t hesitate to communicate with us.
 
GP & GAH

Hey, Linda!

I am writing to you today because I just finished the first volume of my horror comedy comic EVIL CAST and am preparing a pitch document for it. As part of that, I am currently collecting blurbs from fellow writers and or comic/horror peeps to help pitch it + put on the front and back covers (a very tedious process I'm sure you know haha).

I was hoping you'd take a look and, if you liked it, you could share a little blurb with me? All six issues + some info are attached at the end of this email.

Here's an example of what I'm collecting:

"Evil Cast is a clever mix of cosmic creeps and humor. I had a blast with it."
          -Paul Tremblay (Author of A Head Full of Ghosts)

"Fans of horror comedy won't find another comic this entertaining. I want to live in this universe"
          -Sadie Hartmann (SCREAM Magazine, Cemetery Dance)

"Evil Cast defies classification! Is it Horror? Comedy? Action/adventure? Yes! Yes! Yes! Each issue is a new twist and turn and I can't wait to get my hands on the next issue."
          -Chris Lackey (The H.P. Lovecraft Literary Podcast)

HOWEVER, if you end up not liking it or aren't interested at all—or just haven't the time—absolutely no worries! Regardless, keep up the good work with your own writing and projects!

ABOUT THE COMIC: Evil Cast is a love letter to horror, its conventions, and its fans. Think Evil Dead meets Scooby Doo. Created by writer, podcaster, and horror super-fan Kyle Stück (The Night Shift, Humming Fools) and illustrated by Enrico Orlandi, creator of Dark Horse’s The Flower of the Witch, this comic bathed in blood and self-awareness follows fictional versions of Kyle and his longtime collaborator Noah Baslé (Ominous Media) as they find themselves caught up in a horror adventure filled with all the monsters and evil they previously thought to just be stories.

VOLUME 1 (ISSUES 1-6):

Hello! I am a young mom from the Philippines, Christine Catipon. If you are searching for a family to sponsor or help, please pick us. Help us make the rest of 2021 a better year for our small family. Please take time to read my letter so you will understand why we deserve your help. 
Four typhoons in a span of three weeks last year resulted in extreme and serious damages to properties and many families were displaced including ours. And now, we still have not completed the funds for the roof. 

Plus, I have a son who at age five still does not talk and needs the earliest intervention as possible. And this pandemic is hindering us from being able to do so. 

It's impossible to support your family when it rains every day and you have no stable and safe roof because it was blown away in a storm, and you have no money because a pandemic and a typhoon shut almost every opportunity we have left.

Originally, we had our family’s fundraising page for the roof funds.  Aftermath photos of the typhoon were posted on the fundraising page.  But after a year, it was declared unsuccessful and reached the deadline (overdue date) limit so it was closed. I continued to bravely share our story even if no one seemed to notice us. Help us complete the amount needed so we can finally move on and start standing on our own feet from thereon forward.

For now, our roof completion will be put on hold maybe. We need to focus on my little boy's speech. One or two words from him would mean a very great improvement. We really need professional help (speech therapist maybe) so he can get the help he needs. We need more help now, more than ever. Any amount would mean the whole world to us--any amount would go a long way. At this time, we cannot afford it just yet, so solutions we figured:

1. A (stable) job for me and his papa (preferably online) so we could stay home, stay safe and watch over this little boy at the same time

2. A capital for business (online selling for me and maybe as a food/goods delivery stint for his papa)

3. Sell the songs his papa made from 2 years ago (seven songs in total all available in the music platforms) as this is the only property we have right now

Just in case you choose to aid us, here is our fundraiser: https://gogetfunding.com/foralittleboy/

These all will lead to a stable and secured life for a small family on this side of the world, especially to a young little boy.

Please be the miracle we have been praying for to happen. Please help us rebuild what was lost and secure our home. Please help me, help my son to learn how to speak. 

Please help us get our family, especially my 5-year-old son, a chance to get our lives back together and a way to support ourselves from now on. You can LITERALLY help change someone's life today. Thank you so much!

Love and light,
Christine (a young mama trying to provide the life her family deserves)

“No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of another” -Charles D.

PS. If you cannot help us financially through your organization, please help us personally? If still not, maybe I could work for you instead. Very much in need of any work online as soon as possible. Even temporary work opportunities to be able to sustain our daily needs and save for a capital for our goals and baby's therapy. I am very much willing to work hard for any help you could provide us. I may not be the best employee you will hire but with my family as my inspiration, I will definitely do my best. 

May I send my resume, maybe?

Thank you for understanding and more power. Please be my baby's angel.

Dear Linda Addison,

I would like to invite you as a guest speaker to address Apex Writers Group. Many of our writers voted on which experts they’d love to hear from, and your name came up!

Apex is a coalition of about 550 writers who come together to learn about the craft and business of writing. Our writers range from full-time professionals to beginners. Their goals vary from breaking into the publishing field, leveling up to bestseller, or simply selling more books.

We have guest speakers on Saturdays and Mondays for one-hour engagements over Zoom, and during that time you’re invited to speak about whatever you wish--or simply take questions from our writers.

So join us and have fun talking with us about what you’re passionate about, or what makes you excited. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to reach out. We are setting up speakers for December. Would you prefer to speak on a Monday night or Saturday morning?

Sincerely,
David Farland

coverList.title: The Place of Broken Things
coverList.description: Bram Stoker Award(R) winners Linda D. Addison and Alessandro Manzetti use their unique voices to create a dark, surrealistic poetry collection exploring the many ways shattered bodies, minds, and souls endure. They created poems of visionary imagery encompassing death, gods, goddesses and shadowy, Kafkaesque futures by inspiring each other, along with inspiration from others (Allen Ginsberg, Pablo Neruda, Phillis Wheatley, etc.). Construction of The Place started with the first bitten apple dropped in the Garden. The foundation defined by the crushed, forgotten, and rejected. Filled with timeless space, its walls weep with the blood of brutality, the tears of the innocent, and predatory desire. Enter and let it whisper dark secrets to you. Proudly represented by Crystal Lake Publishing--Tales from the Darkest Depths. Interview with the poets: What makes this poetry collection so special? Alessandro: Collaborations are the salt of poetry, can create special, unique blends and flavours. This book is exquisite, in that way. Linda: Collaborations can create remarkable work, whether it's poetry or fiction. Alessandro and I each did a third on our own and then a third together. This book was written with us in completely different time zones (Arizona & Italy), without ego and is the best poetry I've created so far. Tell us more about the theme of this book. Linda: There was no hard rules, we agreed to riff off any of the words in the title: Place; Broken; Thing(s). The real magic is how the book flowed from us, as we allowed our imagination freedom to play, trusting the dark, surrealistic tales told would fit; and they did! Alessandro: Imagine a collage of different places, connected by invisible wires. We play the role of the explorers of that elusive, borderlands world. Why should readers give this book or your work a try? Linda: Our book has unique songs to offer, something we couldn't recreate separately. It stands alone with any work we do in the future because even the poems I wrote by myself were influenced by working in our shared arena in undefinable ways. Alessandro: If you're a curious traveler, ready to walk with us along a trail without markers, this is a good book for you.

coverList.title:
How To Recognize A Demon  
Has Become Your Friend
coverList.description: Who doesn't need to know How To Recognize A Demon Has Become Your Friend? From the first African-American to receive the HWA Bram Stoker award, this award-winning collection of both horror and science fiction short stories and poetry reveals demons in the most likely people (like a jealous ghost across the street) or in unlikely places (like the dimension-shifting dreams of an American Indian). Recognition is the first step, what you do with your friends/demons after that is up to you.

coverList.title: Being Full of Light, Insubstantial
coverList.description: An exciting collection of 100 poems written by the first African-American recipient of the Bram Stoker Award for superior achievement in poetry. Linda Addison is the only author with fiction in three landmark anthologies that celebrate African-American speculative writers: the award-winning anthology Dark Matter: A Century of Speculative Fiction (Warner Aspect), Dark Dreams I and II (Kensington) and Dark Thirst (Pocket Book). This book includes original photography and art by Brian J. Addison.

coverList.title: Consumed, Reduced to Beautiful Grey Ashes
coverList.description:
This collection of poetry received the HWA Bram Stoker award and includes interior illustrations by Marge Simon, full color cover by Colleen Crary, and an introduction by Charlee Jacob

*Consumed, Reduced To Beautiful Grey Ashes* captures the path between things gone bad and transformation. This volume includes both original pieces and reprints from such sources as Edgar: Digested Verse, Dark Regions, and Pirate Writings.

coverList.title: Animated Objects
coverList.description:
This collection of science fiction, fantasy and horror poetry and short stories includes an introduction from Barry N. Malzberg and the short story, Little Red in the Hood, which appeared on Ellen Datlow's Honorable Mention list in Tenth Annual Year s Best Fantasy & Horror.

*Animated Objects* takes you from the Outside to deep Inside Linda Addison s imagination. Each chapter invites the reader to journey into a universe of the fantastic. The path is paved with light and darkness, like life, but the true center lies in The Prelude.

The last section, journal entries, is a peek into the workings of a writer s mind. In entries from 63 hand-written journals lie the beginnings of poems, starts and endings to stories, observations and life lists.

Become part of the journey. In the end, love is all that matters.

coverList.title: Dark Duet
coverList.description: You've heard their voices before, but never like this: from three-time HWA Bram Stoker Award winner Linda D. Addison and multiple Rhysling Award nominee Stephen M. Wilson comes Dark Duet. Two different voices, in harmony, creating verse that sings and moves on the page, taking the reader through time and space on an infinite symphony of self-exploration. Come dance with them and you may find your own song.

coverList.title: Everything Endless
coverList.description: A cosmic collaboration between Science Fiction & Fantasy Association Grand Master Linda D. Addison and visionary versifier Jamal Hodge, Everything Endless, sheds brilliant light in dark times. With themes of creation, cosmos, the macroscopic and the microscopic, this collection tells the story of life itself and expresses fervent hope for a more creative future. Working in conversation, with alternating poems, the authors blend their unique voices and styles into a symphony of startling images. Never forgetting their roots, these Black poets bring the rhythm of call and response alive across the page with the laser focus of 10,000 suns.

freebies.title: One Night At Sheri-Too-Long's Popcorn Bar
freebies.story: "This is a very special day," he says, raising his glass with his six fingered third hand and tapping my glass. Why does this always happen to me? I could go to the loneliest, faraway bar--a place on a planet outside the known universe and some unnamed genetic hybrid will find me. They always treat me like a long lost brother. They talk and talk and talk until I'm all sticky and wet with their words. I discreetly blink a change control code into my three dimensional self-projector implant to create a transformation in my outer displacement. "I'm a lucky guy!" he says smiling, looking straight into my eyes. So transparency doesn't bother this guy. Great. I fade back into the bar's temporal zone just in time for the bartender('s hair) to notice me. Her dark cloak of hair undulates around her body, covering her in a living full length gown. A mass of curls form '??' above her head. I draw '==' on the counter and longingly watch her hair make another Ankle-high Buffalo Bill for me while the bartender carries on a conversation in sign language with a Venusian in a pressurized tank. I begin to imagine what else hair like that could do... "Not only is this a special day, but meeting you here really makes it unforgettable," he says. The remnants of my daydreams scatter to the darker corners of the darkened bar. This guy has to pick now to get friendly. Just when I'm in the process of building up the energy to talk to the bartender; her hair's been giving me erotic daydreams all evening. I was definitely not looking for a pal, I want the bartender('s hair). "Do I know you?" I ask as rudely as I can. I look him up and down. Didn't anyone tell him that polka dots were out of style on this side of the universe and those big, floppy red shoes--where did this guy come from? "I know you're here, you know I'm here. Double knowing. It doesn't get better than this," he says confidently, his orange curly hair bobbing up and down as he nods. Now I know I'm in trouble. I have no idea what he's talking about. So I just stare at him. Then suddenly his words have a startling affect on my subconscious, resulting in an unexpected physical change. I liquefy and pour into the rim around the bar chair. Wet. I knew that was coming. "You're my kind of person," he says and pours into his chair's rim. A drop splashes into me and suddenly we're in direct pipeline mental contact. All matters of fellowship and love floods my mind. Life is good. Rainbows always come out after the rain. A list of words with a heart replacing the letter 'o' begin to march through my mind. I recompose and say, "Just a minute--you can't just go around splashing yourself into strangers." "I thought like that once," he says after recomposing. "But now that I've met you. Well, I can't stay unaffected. You're the best." He reaches out to slap me on the back, but I activate my Portable Matter Contact Repellent and his hand swings through a temporary tunnel in my torso. That's my limit. Accidental mind drips are one thing (and I'm not so sure that drip was an accident), but body touching without so much as an eye-to-eye invitation--that's an outrage! I slide my right hand into my jacket searching for my Guiltless De-molecularizer when a thin filament wraps around my wrist. I look down and it's a strand of the bartender's hair. She's still talking to someone else, but her hair forms the words BE KIND in the air. I can't believe it--a dream come true. Her hair noticed me! Maybe I could retrieve some joy from this evening. If... If I could get rid of this guy and spend some time with the bartender('s hair). I take an empty hand out of my jacket and three strands of hair caress my cheek before the bartender walks to the other end of the bar. This gives me the kind of chills I've been fantasizing about since I first saw her hair in action. It's time to jump to light speed. I have to make this guy go away and I have to do it in a civilized way since her hair made it clear it didn't want me to disperse him into star matter. So this guy's sitting there real impressed with knowing me (I don't know why) and wanting something (I don't know what). His eyes are bright and filled with expectation. I take all my three-dimensional energy, pipe it into a one-way line in his direction and say, "I can see that you want something--that you have a question to ask me." He nods, smiling with a rim of pink teeth around his lower head. He looks around mischievously to see if anyone is listening and leans toward me. I blink and his face had transforms to pasty white with blue eyebrows and a large, red, round nose. "TRICK OR TREAT!" he yells. The force of his words fling me across the room and I adhere to the wall like one of those six pointed Niobium wall hangings. Sticky. Finally. It's kind of relief. He runs out of the bar, laughing loudly. And it takes two hours for the bartender('s hair) to coax me down from the wall. Not the worst two hours of my life, but I'd rather have that kind of stuff done to me in private instead of in front of the gamey crowd of the bar. But sometimes you have to take your treats (or tricks) where you can get them. The End

freebies.story:
Chapter 3, Section 1.3.1a: Maintain an acceptable holo image at all times when visiting the most interesting planet, native-named Earth, in the "Milky Way" galaxy. Neatness and a good fitting image will gain high marks on the believability scale if inadvertently seen by Earth's sentient beings. Several varieties of images have been tested and rated in this galaxy. Certain highly stylized images have been found to invoke agitated states in members of the species. Reference: "Mars Attacks" vid 84.I.77, "Alien" vid series 39.N.5.2. However, there is a wide range of acceptable non-Earth styles to choose from that allow individuality and personal style. Simplicity within the seeded archetypes has found to be most successful. For popular interpretations of these images reference: "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" vid 45.A.3.7, "X-Files" vid series 849.N.4.9. Exceptions to the lists of fashionable images is the favorite earthling Elvis look. A minimal amount of language and behavior imprinting is necessary to become acceptable to the natives. The only restriction is for travelers sensitive to flash light, since this look invokes picture taking from the natives. This image will allow you to travel among the natives freely; however, it is important to keep in mind that this look should only be worn in the Las Vegas sector, to avoid the rippling effects that have resulted from its overuse. See references to multi-media archives, keyword: "Elvis Sightings".

Chapter 7, Section 5.2.9g: Abduction of human beings has been strictly forbidden since the unfortunate incidents with unconscious memory leaks. These leaks have not caused any high level problems and the long term effects have been entertaining; however, they introduce unacceptable risks for the travel program. Reference: all works of Chris Carter starting in the 20th Century vid series 209.Z.4.7. Abduction of other life forms is allowed as long as the entire creature is taken. Although the problems produced by the Geuu taking only internal organs and leaving the external coverings (see section on Bovine Internal Studies) has not resulted in Earth being put on the non-visitory list, we do not want to create additional issues for the Interspatial Uniplacated Traveler's Board (IUTP). Chapter 14, Section 8.4.2v: It is important to establish viable landing sites if planet fall is intended. Studies have found that locations of expected visitation are best since the local natives will have already woven tales to explain any signs of other worldly sightings. Reference maps of Roswell, Grovers Mill, Area 51. Other sectors have been deemed attractive because of their tolerance of aberrant images. Reference layouts of Hollywood, New York City, all locations of Disney World. When visiting it is important to clean up after yourself. The non-littering clause signed by all participants of the traveler's contract will be strictly enforced. Dark matter, hot or cold, in particular must be kept out of this developing galaxy for obvious reasons. Manipulation of native material is strictly forbidden from the sub-molecular level to larger structures. Documented incidents of the breaking of these rules serve as clear examples of what not to do, no matter how visually pleasing. Reference: the Step Pyramid of King Joser in Egypt, which involved the masterful memory imprinting of several generations of natives. Note that the creation of crop circles by vacationers is discouraged unless you hold at least a Level III certificate in topical Terrain soil and plant design. Although amusing in its final result, these kinds of graffiti will no longer be tolerated by IUTP. In conclusion, we expect all vacationers to review the entire Traveler's Guide in any preferred form (visual, eatable, scent, spiked, etc) and commit it to memory. Enjoy! The End

freebies.title: After The Fire
freebies.sub: Published in Dark Voices, 2000; reprinted in Being Full of Light, Insubstantial & Essence magazine 2008
freebies.story:
I lie in the ashes
desire, memories, hope, love—gone
reduced to a same grayness
except for the hint of shape
the sense of what was. How to rebuild
from such fragile dust
What brick can be formed
with these emptied hands? I gather what
the wind does not take
mix with tears, draw a capricious design
on ground willing to take
my final offering. Standing on sooted bare feet
waiting for the cleansing of the next life
dressed in ashes
I spread my arms.

freebies.title: The Barn
freebies.sub: Published in The Edge, 2000; reprinted in Being Full of Light, Insubstantial
freebies.story:
It stands alone
gray wood stripped of paint
doors long gone, the sunlight stabs
through its broken roof
the inner darkness splits into jagged shadows, abandoned, waiting to be torn down
no one will reenter here
memories of life long gone. My womb moans with the ghost
of the broken structure
both emptied, we wait to be torn down.

freebies.title: Inevitable Singularity
freebies.story:
Before
a hand had five fingers, a body two arms,
humans the capacity to love and hate, give and take,
choice, a hidden agenda, created predictable consequences. After
spatial-temporal needs influence body development
common sense comes in a bottle, clocks are meaningless,
ripe for transformation, the universe continues to expand. Before
BLT was bacon, lettuce, tomato on whole-wheat or white
Artificial Intelligence lived in the dreams of scientists and writers,
a fork was a fork, a spoon—a spoon. After
nano-brain-computer interfacing creates food in the stomach,
school children play with critical technologies at recess,
trash becomes precious input to self-evolving systems. Before
becomes After
when the Universe is rewound by the
One Quantum Computer before it is turned on.

freebies.title: Storm of Souls
freebies.sub: Published in Fantastic Stories magazine 2005; Annual Year's Best Fantasy & Horror Honorable Mention; reprinted in Being Full of Light, Insubstantial
freebies.story:
the rain won't stop
endless pounding
breaking down weak roofs
crumbling concrete
opening the wound of earth
slowly removing every path, every road my ears hurt from the echoing
the rain won't stop
my house is melting, brick like butter
the rats laugh and wait
deep inside, the bones cry
more water for the soup the rain won't stop
even when I repent
I promise in strips of skin
in the blood of my unborn
but in this storm of souls
there is no redemption.

freebies.title: Dragon Love
freebies.sub: Published in Being Full of Light, Insubstantial
freebies.story:
Drawn by his fiery strength
I ignore the smoke-filled air
my eyes locked to golden light
in emerald-blue eyes. Our souls were joined
in one night's flight
my legs wrapped tightly
around his long strong neck. We eat outdoors
meals cooked by his sweet breath
I wear a gown of discarded scales
so we can lie together at night.

lessonsBlessings.header:
My life is lessons and blessings. How else to explain the path of life that has taken me from the tough streets of Philly to a quirky house in New York to a house in the desert? Nestled in the midst of strange and wondrous items, I joyfully write even stranger poems and stories.

Each event in my life holds different mixes of lessons and blessings, rarely 50/50. Often the situations that hurt are more lesson than blessing, but both are in the mix. Seeing each painful experience in this way heals the sting, makes me pay attention to the lesson and grow, to bring more light into my life.
lessonsBlessings.poem:
My life
unfolding in unexpected dimensions:
take a skinny, awkward introvert,
mix in books of fables, science-fiction, fantasy, horror
Season with surprising blessings, people:
One taught me to laugh,
another to question everything
This one to know that there are no secrets
That one to see everything is hidden,
I learned to cry with my whole body,
That I am beautiful,
I am eternal,
Even broken,
I can heal,
rise from the ashes of a predestined life
find my authentic path
And know:
Unfolding life is imperfect.
Love the only truth.
Lessons and blessings
the only sanity…

lifePoems.poem: the choice between Love or fear / isn't done just once / but over & over again / because fear can wait / in the cellular memory of flesh / in past emotions' echos
life doesn't present a straight path / some days fall just right / others just fall
putting busy thoughts aside / inviting stillness / my heartbeat emerges
we all carry wounds / love yours / forgive others
today's exercise / the use of words / "I don't know" / as an answer
turn any delay / into a gift / more time / to love your heart
to love without expectation / is to give a gift / without waiting for a return gift-confirmation-acknowledgement / we can bless from afar or up close…
your smile / brings joy / to a universe / in need of such light
in the story of the Universe / your tale continues / to unfold
be the Hero of the Journey / conquer the Dragon / be the Dragon
art is life / life is art / live the masterpiece you are
what if…we are all connected / on this planet / what you do for yourself, you do for me / what would you different this day / would you choose Love or fear?
when another is acting out / become still air, not fire / don't add to flames / because that burns both
the only one / who can hold you back / from your greatness / is you
we are co-creators of this life / with the Universe / what shall we create today?
for all you want / to change in your life / start with unconditional Love of Self
we can't make others / love themselves / but we can show / our Love for them
when the illusion of control is released / waking up to reality becomes possible…
taking time to look around / at all in my heart & life / that I am joyful to have / each and every one of you…
making peace with the past / increases light for the future
healing comes from / loving my wounds, walls / my silent wailing
TGIF / the universe told me / it's thankful every day / for you
deeply thankful / for all the support & love / a blessing for me, returned to you
ignorance is not knowing / denial is / refusing to know
a new day / a new you / what will you do?
it shouldn't be a struggle / to be accepted as equal / but each life lost / reflects the sad reality / & opportunity for evolution…
there are days / that defy words / other than / Thank You!
crisp air / crisp thoughts / warm hugs
children learn from what we do / not what we say / what are you teaching children around you?
wake from busy life / for a moment / to love the wonder / that is You
glass half-full/half-empty? / try being the glass / be empty / be full
children seen & not heard / become adults / who struggle to find their voice…
support love, not fear / by releasing those who are in pain / from our expectations
what Ever you think / you create / what's on your mind at this moment?
The Journey: stumbling & falling / is as important / as running & succeeding
gentle grace shines behind / every cloud of anger, sadness, loss
wanting a reason to bless you / I take a deep breath / ah, there it is
things end / to make space / for new things / to begin
what ever you find lacking / in your life / & the world / Be That…
the Universe / told me / It loves you
sunlight drizzled/ sweet honey on a new day / let's dance until we're dizzy
take the words / Being Perfect / out of the dictionary / try just Being
love is the best gift / start with Self, then from that brilliant center / give to others…
embrace your greatness / for the world is changed / by fearless Love / not loveless fear
before wishing for more things / spend time with what you have / once upon a time / you greatly desired these things also
no one, no thing / governs your destiny / be the Change…
what are you waiting for / to be grateful / love, money, friends? / decide to be grateful / for breath, life & perhaps / other things will come into focus
having Free Will / means having the choice / to heal, change, evolve / don’t accept being what U were / when you can be what U want…
we can’t control the world / but we can keep returning to Love inside / from fear / some days that might be with each breath
be curious, not critical / of others who are different / this is the Way / of Love, not fear…
in the choice between Love & fear / it’s important to recognize / actions of those feeding fear / & fight to support Love…
expectation is the dream killer / do not be driven / by what U or others expect / be driven by your Dream…
eternal gratitude / to everyone in my life / each moment of joy & tears / are breathless lessons, blessings…
do not be defined-limited / by anyone, including your fear / instead be driven by your dreams…
as 1 year ends / another begins / commit to increase Love-Kindness / decreasing fear / in myself & the world @day...
know that when someone feels less inside / they find ways to put down others / increasing fear with their lack of self-love…
today, relax in gratitude / tomorrow, is coming…
Love is in the air – the ground – your fingertips – your smile!
free will / we are free to think / whatever we want / but take care / what you speak

do not give your joy / to headlines designed / to increase fear / for it is
through fear / your light is stolen…

in this time of division & destabilization / recognize & embrace your
reactions / find space to let sunlight in / know you aren’t alone / we are
many…

living isn’t about / Not making mistakes or Not feeling defeated / living
is about / allowing those feelings / then learning & trying
Again-Again-Again…

if someone says you are less / by some ruler they use / it says nothing
about you / & everything about it their weak egos…

we are One / in spite of others / trying to erase some, / no human is less
or more / than another…

each new day / a fresh start / to the rest of our life / where all is
possible…

onlineResourceLinks.text: Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers of America, Inc (SFWA)
Ultimate SF Web Guide (hub of SF resources)

onlineResources.header: Amazon and Other Online Book Stores

publications.title: 2021 SFPA Rhysling Anthology
publications.text: The Best Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror Poetry of 2020, includes my poem, Summer Time(lessness)

publications.title: Black Panther: Tales of Wakanda
publications.text: A ground-breaking anthology celebrating Marvel’s beloved Black Panther and his home of Wakanda, penned by an all-star cast of authors

publications.title: Don't Turn Out the Lights: A Tribute to Alvin Schwartz's Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark.
publications.text: Flesh- hungry ogres ? Brains full of spiders ? Haunted houses you can’t escape ? This collection of 35 terrifying stories from the Horror Writers Association has it all, including ghastly illustrations from Iris Compiet that will absolutely chill readers to the bone.

publications.title: Miscreations: Gods, Monstrosities & Other Horrors
publications.text: What happens when we make monsters? What happens when we make monsters of ourselves? Grotesque beings lurch from our darkest dreams. (Edited by Doug Murano and Michael Bailey)

publications.title: The Dystopian States of America: A Charity Anthology Benefiting the ACLU Foundation
publications.text: Features dystopian views of the future, for America and/ or the entire world. (edited by Matt Bechtel)

publications.title: The Twisted Book of Shadows
publications.text: Within these pages you will find the beautifully weird side- by - side with terrifying nightmares, horrifying folklore, and hellish futures, with an introduction by Linda D.Addison. (edited by Christopher Golden, James A.Moore)

publications.title: Black Celebration: Amazing Articles on African American Horror
publications.text: A collection of articles, essays and interviews with and by African American horror writers on black representation in horror, horror diversity, reviews of African American horror films, horror novels, weird fiction, dark fantasy and more.

publications.title: 100+ Black Women in Horror Writing
publications.text: Biographies of over one hundred black women who write horror, interviews with 17 of these women and an essay by David Watson on LA Banks and Octavia Butler.

publications.title: 2018 Rhysling Anthology
publications.text: The Best Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror Poetry of 2017 (edited by Linda D. Addison)

publications.title: Blacktastic!
publications.text: The official anthology of Blacktasticon 2018, offers a tantalizing glimpse into the imagination of its writers. This the beginning of an amazing journey into the Black Fantastic!

publications.title: Cosmic Underground: A Grimoire of Black Speculative Discontent and its inspiration
publications.text: The ground-breaking exhibition Unveiling Visions, applies a global lens and planetary vision to the black imagination, and brings this context to a wide survey of contemporary works.

publications.title: Dark Voices
publications.text: 100% of profits from this Lycan Valley Charity Anthology will go to benefit breast cancer non-profit organizations.

publications.title: It's Alive: Bringing Your Nightmares to Life
publications.text: Focuses on learning the craft in order to take your story from concept to completion.

publications.title: Scary Out There
publications.text: Multiple Bram Stoker Award–winning author Jonathan Maberry compiles more than twenty stories and poems, written by members of the Horror Writers Association, in this terrifying collection about our worst fears.

publications.title: Sycorax's Daughters
publications.text: A 2018 HWA Bram Stoker Award Finalist! Thought-provoking, powerful, and revealing, this anthology is composed of 28 dark stories and 14 poems written by African-American women writers.

publications.title: Into Painfreak
publications.text: Featuring all new work from some of the top authors in modern horror and includes an all new novelette from Edward Lee! This book takes us deep, deep into the bowels of Painfreak, the traveling club that arises out of the dark and calls to those seeking the ultimate in pleasure and pain. (edited by Gerard Houarner)

publications.title: The Beauty of Death
publications.text: HWA Bram Stoker Award Finalist - Superior Achievement in an anthology. Over 40 stories and novellas by both contemporary masters of horror and exciting newcomers. (edited by Bram Stoker Award® Winning Author Alessandro Manzetti)

publications.title: The Original Van Gogh's Ear Anthology online
publications.text: Includes Linda Addison’s poem 'Empathy.'

publications.title: High Stakes
publications.text: Ten thrilling new vampire tales from award-winning authors explore the world of the undead and the twisted games they play, not only with their prey, but with each other. Poem by Linda Addison. (edited by Gabrielle Faust)

publications.title: How Geek Girls Will Rule the World
publications.text: Features interviews with famous women in the fields of computer science, science and mathematics, gaming, science fiction and fantasy, and comics and manga to learn how they overcame any sexism they experienced to get where they are today. (by Jennifer Thorpe-Moscon, PhD)

publications.title: Slices of Flesh: Do you like your horror in small bite-sized chunks?
publications.text: These flash fiction stories oozed from the brains of some of the best horror writers from around the world and will fit perfectly into your daily diet of "scary."

publications.title: Dark Faith
publications.text: The destructiveness of passion, both earthly and supernatural, makes cities bleed and souls burn across worlds, through endless time. (edited by Maurice Broaddus

publications.title: Genesis: An Anthology of Black Science Fiction
publications.text: Delve into the worlds of science fiction, speculative fiction, horror and fantasy by writers seasoned and up and coming with stories that will capture your imaginations like never before.

publications.title: Big Book of Necon
publications.text: (edited by Bob Booth)

publications.title: Dark Thirst: A haunting anthology of vampire fiction
publications.text: A volume that brings a colorful new dimension to one of the world's most erotic and enduring myths, featuring stories from some of today’s most popular African-American writers.

publications.title: The 2nd Coming: Volume 2 of The Best of Pirate Writings
publications.text: Featuring science fiction & fantasy collected from the pages of Pirate Writings magazine.

publications.title: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, May/June
publications.text: My first appearance with my poem, The Un-Awakened (Octavia E. Butler 1947-2006; edited by Sheree Renée Thomas)

publications.title: Weird Tales Magazine #364
publications.text: This issue features 13 works of horror and dark fantasy by masters of the craft. (Edited by Jonathan Maberry)

publications.title: SFPA Star*Line 43.4 All Black issue
publications.text: To promote the Black Speculative Arts Movement. (Edited by Melanie Stormm, cover artist Ross Browne)

publications.title: Terror Tract, April 2020
publications.text: 17 dark poems and stories come together to make you scream.

publications.title: Uncanny Magazine
publications.text: Safe Havens—WFC Award 2018 Ceremony Toastmaster Speech by Linda D. Addison.

publications.title: Apex Magazine #95
publications.text: Monthly science fiction, fantasy, and horror magazine featuring original, mind-bending short fiction from many of the top pros of the field. (Editor Maurice Broaddus)

publications.title: Eye to the Telescope Magazine #25
publications.text: A quarterly online journal, publishes science-fiction, fantasy, horror, and other speculative poetry. This issue's theme was "Garbage." (Edited by John Reinhart, theme=Garbage)

publications.title: Dark Discoveries Magazine #34
publications.text: A quarterly magazine. This issue's theme was "Vampyre."

publications.title: Spectral Realms Magazine #3
publications.text: A number of leading contemporary authors of weird fiction step up to contribute poems of strangeness and terror. (Edited by S. T. Joshi)

publications.title: Abyss & Apex Magazine
publications.text: My poem, Dico, King of Hat Tricks, from Dark Duet collection.

publications.title: Under Twin Suns
publications.text: Authors share their harrowing visions of worlds shaped by the Yellow Sign, in stories and poems inspired by Robert W. Chambers's foundational works of weird horror.

publications.title: Were Tales: A Shapeshifter Anthology
publications.text: A collection of scary, thrilling, dark, mysterious, and even humorous tales and poems of shapeshifters, edited by S. D. Vassallo & Steven M. Long; contains my poem, "The Butterfly Affect."

publications.title: Southwest Review Magazine, 2021 Fall Issue
publications.text: Has a Halloween poem of mine in it, "D2D Candy Corn."

publications.title: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, Sept/Oct
publications.text: Contains two of my poems, inspired by Edgar Allan Poe (The Conqueror Wormhole; Sonnet_To MetaScience).

publications.title: Giving The Devil His Due (Running Wild Press)
publications.text: All net proceeds from sales of this anthology go toward supporting The Pixel Project's anti-violence against women programs; contains my story, *Finding Water to Catch Fire*.

publications.title: Writers Workshop of Horror 2
publications.text: A collection of essays and interviews focusing on the art and craft of writing horror and dark fantasy, edited by Michael Knost, contains my essay: "Fearful Poetry"

publications.title: Bridging Worlds anthology
publications.text: Global conversations on creating Pan-African Speculative Literature in a Pandemic, contains my essay: Expect the Unexpected—WTH? (free download)

publications.title: Trouble the Waters anthology
publications.text: Gathers the tidal force of writers from Lagos to New Orleans, Memphis to Copenhagen, Northern Ireland and London, offering extraordinary speculative fiction tales of ancient waters in all its myriad forms, contains my poem: Mami Wata, Goddess of Clear Blue.

publications.title: Infectious Hope: Poems of Hope & Resilience from the Pandemic
publications.text: This poetry anthology includes a spectacular range of diverse poets from around the globe, and focuses on their insights and strength during the pandemic, contains my poem: Here/Now.

publications.title: Attack from the 80s
publications.text: This anthology has new tales of slumber party horrors, VCR monsters, and problems that can't be solved with a smart phone, contains my poem: Return of the Reanimated Nightmare.

publications.title: A Haunted History of Invisible Women
publications.text: Edited by Leanna Renee Hieber, Andrea Janes, Elizabeth Kerri Mahon, includes my Afterword

publications.title: A Woman Unbecoming
publications.text: Edited by Rachel A. Brune & Carol Gyzander, includes my poem, Failed Love Lessons

publications.title: Chiral Mad 5
publications.text: Edited by Michael Bailey, includes my poem, Seven Symptoms of the End/Beginning/End/Beginning

publications.title: Conjuring Worlds: An Afrofuturist Textbook for Middle and High School Students
publications.text: Includes a lesson based on my poem, The Cosmic Adventures of Jar Boy

publications.title: Foundlings by Cindy O'Quinn, Stephanie Ellis
publications.text: Found poetry inspired by Alessandro Manzetti and I, we wrote the Foreword

publications.title: Human Monsters
publications.text: Edited by Sadie Hartmann & Ashley Saywers, includes my poem, Me & My Shadow

publications.title: HWA Other Terrors
publications.text: Edited by Vince A Liaguno, Rena Mason, include my poem, Illusions of the De-Evolved

publications.title: Hybrid: Misfits, Monsters and Other Phenomena
publications.text: Includes my poem, Fracking-lution

publications.title: Predator: Eyes of the Demon
publications.text: Edited by Bryan Thomas Schmidt with my story, Proving Ground

publications.title: The 2022 Rhysling Anthology
publications.text: Has two of my poems nominated for the SFPA Rhysling award, The Conqueror Worm(Hole) & The Butterfly Affect (won Third Place—Short Poem Category)

publications.title: The DRABBUN Anthology
publications.text: Includes my drabbun, The Fixer

publications.title: Traveling the Spaceways
publications.text: Edited by Sheree Renée Thomas, includes my poems, Animation & Land Sharks

publications.title: Under Her Skin
publications.text: Edited by Lindy Ryan, Toni Miller, contains my Foreword

publications.title: Writing Poetry in the Dark
publications.text: Includes my essay, Writing Speculative Poetry in Experimental Forms & my poem, In the Light and Dark of Blood

publications.title: Apex Magazine #130
publications.text: Contains my essay Never Let The Light Out

publications.title: Speculative North Magazine #6
publications.text: Includes my poems Nightshift & Whale Riding

publications.title: Uncanny Magazine, Issue 48
publications.text: Includes my poem: The Construct’s Co-Emergence

publications.title: Black Fire—This Time
publications.text: An anthology that explores all facets of the Black Arts Movement. Edited by Dr. Kim McMillon and Kofi Antwi, contains my poems: MetaGender Machine, Neo-Americans.

publications.title: Classic Monsters Unleashed
publications.text: Stories of famous monsters in a new horror anthology, contains my story: Da Noise_Da Funk_Da Blob.

publications.title: Attack from the ’80s anthology (paperback)
publications.text: The paperback format of this anthology has tales of slumber party horrors, VCR monsters, and problems that can't be solved with a smart phone, contains my poem: Return of the Reanimated Nightmare.

publications.title: Daughter of Sarpedon anthology
publications.text: Edited by Heather & S.D. Vassallo, short stories, poems, and drabbles about Medusa, ranging from retellings to completely new work, from ancient to modern day.

publications.title: Black Panther: Tales of Wakanda (paperback)
publications.text: A ground-breaking anthology celebrating Marvel’s beloved Black Panther and his home of Wakanda, penned by an all-star cast of authors, includes my story Shadow Dreams.

publications.title: Black Cat Weekly Magazine #28
publications.text: Mystery, Crime, SF, Fantasy fiction, includes my story Milez To Go.

publications.title: Black Cat Weekly Magazine #49
publications.text: Mystery, Crime, SF, Fantasy fiction, includes my story The Power.

publications.title: Sorghum & Spear Anthology - The Way of Silk and Stone
publications.text: In a world created by Dedren Snead, edited by Sheree Renée Thomas, foreword by Nisi Shawl, dedicated to Valjeanne Jeffers & Nichelle Nichols, includes my poem, The Messenger.

publications.title: A Unioverse Anthology: Stories of the Reconvergence
publications.text: In the year 2145 AD, Malcolm Orion, destined to go down in history as the Brave Traveler, made his historic jump through space, launching his consciousness across the universe. 500 years later, worlds long isolated from each other are once again connected. This anthology presents tales of this reconvergence, edited by Angie Hodapp and Joshua Viola, includes my poem Relentless Realities & Impossible Intention.

publications.title: Shakespeare Unleashed
publications.text: This anthology reimagines the Bard’s greatest works as short horror stories…as well as horror sonnets, edited by  James Aquilone, includes my sonnet, Not From My Heart Do I Your Judgement Pluck.

publications.title: The Book of Witches
publications.text: This extraordinary anthology vividly breathes life into one of the most captivating and feared magical sorceresses, edited by Jonathan Strahan, includes my poem Seed of Power.

publications.title: 2023 Black Women in Horror Magazine Special Edition
publications.text: This is the ONLY place you can access the Premium FULL COLOR magazine for download or online viewing. Click the image to get your copy today, includes my poem Secret Places.

publications.title: Weird Tales: 100 Years of Weird anthology
publications.text: Celebrating the 100th anniversary of the first issues of Weird Tales Magazine, this masterful compendium of new and classic stories, flash fiction, essays, and poems from the giants of speculative fiction edited by by Jonathan Maberry, includes my poem How to Make the Animal Perfect?

publications.title: Deathrealm: Spirits anthology
publications.text: 20 all new stories and poems by the most intense voices ever to weave their way into your waking world edited by Stephen Mark Rainey, includes my poem, As Below, So Above

publications.title: Project Muse Poe Studies vol. 56
publications.text: African American Writers Respond to Poe by John C. Gruesser, Norlisha Crawford and others, includes an interview with me and my poem, On My Own (Inspired by Edgar Allan Poe's Alone).

publications.title: The Drive-In: Multiplex anthology
publications.text: 21 writers pay tribute to Lansdale with new stories and novellas set in the bizarre and terrifying universe created by the champion mojo storyteller his own self, all those years ago, includes my piece, Things As They Seem, What Could Be & Everything Improbable.

publications.title: Qualia Nous Vol 2
publications.text: An anthology of dark science fiction and fantasy edited by Michael Bailey and featuring artwork throughout by Pat R. Steiner, includes my poem, Shattered in Daylight.

publications.title: 160 Black Women in Horror
publications.text: Biographies of 160 black women who write horror, essays about Valjeanne Jeffers, L.A. Banks and Carolyn Saulson; was assembled by Sumiko Saulson and Kenya Moss-Dyme. This book was initially compiled by Sumiko Saulson in honor of Black Women in Horror during February (Black History Month) and March (Women in History Month) and is an extension of a series that started out as a project for Women in Horror Month back in February 2013.

publications.title: 2023 SFPA Rhysling Anthology
publications.text: The Best Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror Poetry of 2022, includes my poem, Fracing-lution.

publications.title: The Lore of Inscrutable Dreams by Colleen Anderson
publications.text: A speculative poetry journey into the depths of the human experience, exploring themes of female empowerment, forging one’s own path, and the power of fairytales and magic within us, contains my introduction, Daydreams of the Unexplainable.

publications.title: Circles in the Hair anthology
publications.text: A free anthology by the members of the writers group CITH, edited by Faith L. Justice and Gordon Linzner, features stories set in times as distant as Bronze Age China and the far flung future; in places as strange as a Brooklyn courthouse and the edge of the universe. These stories and poems evoke laughter, tears, shivers, and thoughtfulness, includes three poems by me. Forward by Nancy Kress and Afterword by Terry Bisson.

publications.title: Weird Tales magazine edited by Jonathan Maberry: The Bram Stoker Awards issue #369
publications.text: This issue celebrates the Bram Stoker Awards, the Oscars of the horror trade. They are presented every year by the Horror Writers Association, a group founded in 1985 (and incorporated in 1987) by a collective of masters of that genre, including Joe R. Lansdale, Karen Lansdale, Robert McCammon, and Dean Koontz edited by Jonathan Maberry, includes my poem, The Time Less Gambit.

publications.title: Playlist of the Damned anthology edited by Jess Landry and Willow Dawn Becker
publications.text: This anthology inspired by music has possessed rock stars, killer radio stations, and concerts from the depths of hell. A macabre musical feast, it includes 300 pages of terrifying, bizarre stories about the hypnotic power of music, includes my poem Red, Black & Blue.

publications.title: Folk Horror Short Stories edited by Paul Kane and Marie O’Regan
publications.text: A new anthology of Folk Horror stories, covering a wide range of mythologies and dark corners from around the world, revealing tales from the shadows of isolation, creepy forests and horrors rising from the land itself, includes my poem Ghost Land of Giants.

publications.title: Bestiary of Blood anthology edited by Jamal Hodge
publications.text: This modern anthology of animal/predator horrors inspired by the timeless tales of Aesop’s Fables, modernized for a more complex, unforgiving world, includes my story The Tale of the Twin Stars, Born of Earth and Sea and my poem The Large Reckoning.

publications.title: Rock Stars of Horror Collectors Cards
publications.text: Each 5×7 inch Rock Stars of Horror Collector Cards features a gorgeous piece of art, gold foil stamping, and a never before seen piece of flash fiction printed on high quality, glossy archival stock and comes with a Certificate of Authenticity and protective folder at no additional cost, includes my story The Cost of Salvation.

publications.title: Interdimensions 2024 Stories from the Gen Con Writers Symposium edited by Tonya Kristen Finley
publications.text: Sixteen brand new tales from guests of the 2024 Gen Con Writers Symposium take you on a journey spanning the genres of fantasy, science fiction, horror, and slipstream, includes my story All Time is Now.

publications.title: Shadows and Verse anthology edited by Jonathan Maberry
publications.text: A very special collection of poems and song lyrics that explore darkness in all its many form,  the supernatural, grief, PTSD, loss, the unknown, death, and even joy, includes my commentary on Langston Hughes’s poem: Sick Room.

publications.title: The Unholy Trinity fiction collection by L. Marie Wood
publications.text: The Unholy Trinity combines L. Marie Wood horror collections, Caliginy, Phantasma, and Anathema into one volume of quiet, extreme, and dark horror, psychological thrillers, and rousing suspense that will keep you teetering on the edge of your seat, includes my Foreword.

publications.title: You’re Not Alone in the Dark anthology edited by Eugene Johnson and Eric Guignard
publications.text: This blockbuster non-fiction anthology features interviews, excerpts, essays exploring mental health in the horror writer community, includes my interview.

publications.title: A Place Between Waking and Forgetting, fiction collection by Eugen Bacon
publications.text: This incredible book includes my introduction, Forgetting, Walking Between

reviewsQuotes.text: *HOW TO RECOGNIZE A DEMON HAS BECOME YOUR FRIEND* is a book rich in diversity. The intellectual and emotional themes in this book range from the subtle to the sublime. It embraces everything from childhood innocence to childhood abuse as well as an adults yearning for acceptance to an adults acceptance of identity lost. And Addison weaves these themes in equally varying styles and genres; her creativity manifesting itself in the forms of science fiction, flash fiction, horror fiction, fantasy fiction, and poetry. When it comes to writing styles, Linda Addison might be a Jack Of All Trades, but I can say after reading this collection, she is damn good at all of them.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: TT Zuma, *Horror World*, November 2011

reviewsQuotes.text: *HOW TO RECOGNIZE A DEMON HAS BECOME YOUR FRIEND*... Edgy and sparkling language depicts the demons that lurk all around us and, most importantly, within us. Bright as a star and sharp as a diamond, Linda Addison takes us on a tour de force through the dark latitudes of the demonic, imparting valuable knowledge and marvelous entertainments.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: J.L. Comeau, *Creature Feature Tomb of Horror*, December 2011

reviewsQuotes.text: *HOW TO RECOGNIZE A DEMON HAS BECOME YOUR FRIEND* leans on the dark fantasy/horror side and is sprinkled generously with some nifty (and at times funny) sci-fi. My favorite poems include Land Sharks, an inventive and fun urban fantasy of sorts (and originally appeared in an issue of the famous Asimov's SF Magazine), Comic Cannibals, Demon Dance, and the title piece also display the author's skill at dark verse. There are many more tales and poems here, and not a slow one in the bunch. This is a fine introduction to Addison's world and a trip well worth taking.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Nick Cato, *The Horror Fiction Review*, March 2012

reviewsQuotes.text: Linda Addison’s third book of poems, *BEING FULL OF LIGHT, INSUBSTANTIAL*, is, contrary to its title, most substantial indeed. It’s a masterful assortment of over one hundred poems, most of them original to this book, full of joy and sorrow, wisdom and compassion, and close observation of life. Perhaps the key phrase to sum up its tenor is "hopeful, appreciative, wondering and caring." Addison treats of metaphysics, but also of topical matters such as 9/11, Katrina and New Orleans, and war. She’s both fantastical—as in "Mermaid in the Bronx"—and mimetic, as in "The Barn." Anyone who can make you believe in a pickled embryo as an enticing protagonist ("The Cosmic Adventures of Jar Boy") is a master wordsmith indeed.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Paul De Filippo, *Asimov’s Science Fiction* magazine, July 2008

reviewsQuotes.text: With an unusual blend of lyricism and concentrated detail, Linda Addison offers up her distinctive poetic skills that are unlike any you've encountered elsewhere. *BEING FULL OF LIGHT, INSUBSTANTIAL* is poetic achievement as solid and well-founded as a palace cornerstone. And that palace rings with the thrum and cadence of voice, weaving tales and songs full of fantasy and myth that will sweep you down from the eaves and up to the towers.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Tom Piccirilli, award winning author of *THE MIDNIGHT ROAD*

reviewsQuotes.text: There is something otherworldly and magical about Linda Addison's poetry, as though she is a primordial force of nature who can see to the very bottom of the oceans and to the very end of the universe. From "Falling Away": Falling away from Earth/releasing time and pain/an exhalation of demons/wait to chew at bones left behind/ … begins one of the finest contemplations of the end of corporeal existence I've ever encountered. *BEING FULL OF LIGHT, INSUBSTANTIAL* is a major poetry collection by a major American poet whose talent seems to grow exponentially with each collection she's published. Includes breathtaking photo-art by Brian James Addison.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: J.L. Comeau, award winning short story writer

reviewsQuotes.text: Addison's poems bring out images of a person struggling to chip away the confining nature of our modern times in order to go back to a spiritual existence that is the basis of life. Linda D. Addison has a mesmerizing control of the language and effortlessly reconstructs the past, present and future giving the reader something to digest and ponder.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Joey Pinkney, *C&B Books*

reviewsQuotes.text: [Linda] brings a tight focus to small, intimate details which in turn illuminate and echo larger concerns. What I like about her work is that it reads like the observations you might get from a friend, albeit a friend with a gift of language and insight, who’s been let into a few more secrets about what’s out there in the world than the rest of us have experienced
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Charles De Lint, *Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction*

reviewsQuotes.text: With studied control and subtle perception, Linda’s poems are luminous—wet, whole 'shiny things' that blaze long after the pages are turned.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Sheree Renée Thomas, award winning editor of *Dark Matter: Reading the Bones*

reviewsQuotes.text: Addison has an amazing lyrical sense, juxtaposing seemingly unrelated images—like a mundane house cleaning list and the necessary ingredients to passion and a healthy life—in one taut, no-syllable-wasted poem.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: John Everson, Bram Stoker nominee

reviewsQuotes.text: Linda Addison plays fresh variations on the voodoo theme in "The Power." [story from *Dark Dreams I*]
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Publishers Weekly

reviewsQuotes.text: Linda Addison’s *CONSUMED, REDUCED TO BEAUTIFUL GREY ASHES*, [is] a strong sophomore effort, contains such gems as "The Morpheus Calculation," which postulates a redemptive apocalypse in shimmering, subtle lines.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Paul De Filippo, *Asimov’s Science Fiction* magazine, December 2002

reviewsQuotes.text: Addison has enough invention for two writers, and enough heart for three.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Terry Bisson, Nebula Award winning author

reviewsQuotes.text: Ranging from despair to transformation, Ms. Addison speaks to the human condition, her words igniting empathetic personal, often painful, emotion... joy to read, filled with vivid imagery and grace.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Shannon Reilly, *Morbid Musings*

reviewsQuotes.text: This collection [*CONSUMED, REDUCED TO BEAUTIFUL GREY ASHES*] reads like a string of pearls, with images that recur in poem after poem, reminding us of theme in the most subtle manner. The message penetrates and lingers long after the final poem has been consumed.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Jacquline Jones LaMon, *AALBC.com* & *African Voices*

reviewsQuotes.text: ...let Linda prove that inspired poetry can be more moving, and horrifying, than even the best-written novel.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Garrett Peck, *Cemetery Dance*

reviewsQuotes.text: Linda Addison's "Twice, At Once, Separated&;quot [from *DARK MATTER I*] has, almost uniquely among the new stories, a recognizable sci-fi setting (a generation ship sailing between the stars); but its characters live as traditional Yanomami tribes people, and the story—a dream-impelled journey of self-discovery—possesses the feel of fantasy.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Gregory Feeley, *The Washington Post*

reviewsQuotes.text: Linda Addison pours heart and soul upon the page in her first collection [*ANIMATED OBJECTS*]. A freshet of poems, journal entries, and stories, this book shows the birth and early maturity of the author. Most affecting to my sensibilities was her [story] "Dust to Dust", which exactly recaptures—not, I believe, out of conscious homage, but out of similar soul-stirrings—Lord Dunsany’s "Where the Tides Ebb and Flow." Think it’s easy writing a story from a corpse’s point of view? Only because Addison beguiles you so.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Paul De Filippo, *Asimov’s Science Fiction* magazine

reviewsQuotes.text: ...reveals the little horrors of the days, the curiously individual science fictions of the nights, the fantasies where 'tomorrow will be reborn'
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Charlee Jacob

reviewsQuotes.text: With the eloquent simplicity of the writers of ancient earth tales, and the pop cleverness of modern-day fantasists, Linda Addison shares with the reader a collection [*ANIMATED OBJECTS*] from her very human, very mystical realm; images often tender, poignant, brutal, transcendent.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Elizabeth Massie, Bram Stoker Award winning author

reviewsQuotes.text: *ANIMATED OBJECTS* is a lively collection that ranges from the wry and amusing to raw, primal emotion. Its works sometimes tickle and at other times cut, taking the reader from joy to despair, reality to fantasy, and in the end affirming that the journey is, indeed, worthwhile.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Gerard Daniel Houarner, *Pirate Writings* magazine

reviewsQuotes.text: *ANIMATED OBJECTS* is not only a tour de force but also a tour through the material and raw core of the poet herself, who invites the reader in to bear witness to a life that is comprised of both sensitive retrospect and worldly affirmation.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Tom Piccirilli, "Pic's Picks" for *Barnes & Noble/Epitaph* magazine

reviewsQuotes.text: ...Both amusing and painful, rooted in darkness and the alien, *ANIMATED OBJECTS* reaffirms that life is worth living, love worth risking, and that you can grow wings to carry you higher. It's inspirational.
reviewsQuotes.attribution: Paula Guran, *DarkEcho Newsletter*
